explanation: The last chapter of the Bible containing prophecies about the end of the world, the day of judgment, and the final victory over evil.
A sequence of seven divine warnings or judgments blown by angels to bring disasters upon the earth.
Symbols of heavenly beings, often interpreted as fallen angels or powers in the cosmic battle between good and evil.
The term used for the evil spirits (an army of horses) that have power to kill a third of humanity with their stings, poisonous bites, and fire-breathing tails.
The name of the destroyer or angel of death who rules over the evil spirits in the judgment of the seventh trumpet.
The Greek word for "destroyer," the title given to the same being as Abaddon, emphasizing his role as a bringer of ruin.
The fraction of the earth or humanity struck by each individual disaster in the trumpets, indicating a partial but not complete judgment at this point.
